blocks.text:
The programme combines Brazil’s famous landmarks with places you may miss on a short first visit. On your free day in Rio, you can choose a boat trip on Guanabara Bay, a helicopter flight, the Botanical Garden, a favela tour or an evening in Lapa. At Iguazu, you can add a Macuco Safari, the Bird Park and dinner with a show at Rafain Grill Place. City panoramas give way to ocean beaches, tropical forest, vast waterfalls and the green hills of the Coffee Valley. History runs through the journey too, from Rio’s old centre to the houses and working buildings of the coffee estates.

## Tour highlights

In Rio, you will go up Sugar Loaf and Corcovado to the statue of Christ the Redeemer. From above, you can see Copacabana, Ipanema, Guanabara Bay, the mountains and the city neighbourhoods that reach right down to the ocean.

The historic centre reveals another side of Rio: the 18th-century Candelária Church, São Bento Monastery, the Municipal Theatre, the Imperial Palace and the Metropolitan Cathedral. You can plan your free day around your interests, from a quiet walk in the Botanical Garden to a helicopter flight over the city.

At Iguazu Falls, you will visit both sides of the border. The Brazilian side gives you a broad panorama of the cascades, while the Argentine side takes you along several walking trails close to the water and to the Devil’s Throat.

The final part of the journey focuses on the Coffee Valley. The estates of 19th-century coffee barons, their old buildings and the history of the plantations have been preserved here. You finish with a tasting of freshly brewed Brazilian coffee.
